headline: Town Meeting approved a $71.1 million budget, $25 million for road repairs, an $8.8 million middle school roof, and appointed clerk status.
synopsis: At the April 2026 Annual and Special Town Meetings, Southborough voters approved a $71.1 million FY27 municipal operating budget along with major borrowing authorizations for municipal infrastructure. Voters authorized $25 million in borrowing for roadway and sidewalk improvements, $8.8 million for replacing the Trottier Middle School roof, and voted to transition the town clerk from an elected to an appointed position. Town Meeting also adopted new industrial park zoning standards for data centers and expanded accessory dwelling units up to 1,200 square feet by right, while rejecting a two-family dwelling amendment. Outside of Town Meeting, the Elementary School Building Committee selected Tappe Architects for the Neary School feasibility study, and both local school committees voted to opt out of interdistrict school choice. In development reviews, the Zoning Board of Appeals closed its public hearing on a 32-unit Chapter 40B development at 250 Turnpike Road.

top_items.title: $25 million road and sidewalk borrowing approved
top_items.why: Town Meeting approved up to $25 million in borrowing to fund a multi-year road repair plan and four new sidewalks. Debt exclusion questions were placed on the May annual town election ballot.
top_items.body: Voters passed Article 13 to address ongoing deterioration across 72 miles of town roadways using a 20-year borrowing authorization. A floor amendment seeking to mandate state invasive species guidelines and certified weed-free soil was defeated before the final vote.

top_items.title: Town Meeting adopts $71.1 million FY27 operating budget
top_items.why: Voters approved a $71,077,130 general fund municipal budget, raising $66,917,959 through taxation.
top_items.body: Budget lines for police staffing, employee benefits, and the Economic Development Committee were held for separate debate before the full operating budget passed. Officials outlined department staffing levels and discussed high-deductible health plan offerings intended to reduce municipal health benefit costs.

top_items.title: $8.8 million borrowing approved for Trottier School roof
top_items.why: Town Meeting authorized $8,833,964 in borrowing to replace the leaking roof at Trottier Middle School. The borrowing is contingent on debt exclusion approval at the May town election.
top_items.body: The Massachusetts School Building Authority will reimburse up to 41.32 percent of eligible project costs. The Select Board, School Committee, and Advisory Committee all supported the project to resolve active roof leaks.

top_items.title: Town Clerk converted from elected to appointed office
top_items.why: Special Town Meeting approved Article 1 to make the town clerk an appointed position rather than an elected one.
top_items.body: Former clerk Jim Hegarty explained that increasing election and statutory complexities make appointment by the Select Board based on professional qualifications preferable. A floor amendment to block the town from petitioning the state legislature for a special act failed, and the main article passed by majority vote.

top_items.title: Accessory dwelling units expanded up to 1,200 square feet
top_items.why: Town Meeting approved Article 29 to allow accessory dwelling units up to 1,200 square feet by right, lifting the prior 50 percent gross floor area restriction.
top_items.body: The Zoning Board of Appeals sponsored the measure to provide flexibility for smaller homes and family caregivers. The Advisory Committee recommended against approval due to concerns over neighborhood density and septic capacity, but voters approved the expansion.

top_items.title: Tappe Architects chosen for Neary School feasibility study
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted unanimously to select Tappe Architects for contract negotiations to conduct the Neary School feasibility study.
top_items.body: Following interviews with Arrowstreet, RGB Architects, and Tappe Architects, the committee favored Tappe's public school track record and approach to balancing renovation options with tight cost constraints. Member Andrew Pfaff was designated to participate in contract negotiations alongside administrative reference checks.

top_items.title: Hearing closed on 250 Turnpike Road 40B project
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals closed the public hearing on a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit for 32 rental townhomes at 250 Turnpike Road.
top_items.body: The board and peer reviewers discussed culvert dimensions for wildlife passage, retaining wall setbacks near the 20-foot wetland buffer, and stormwater drainage models. Deliberations on the application and decision conditions were scheduled for May 6.
